questions.prompt: Two threads run bins[v] = bins[v] + 1 (not atomic) at the same time on the same v. What can happen?
options: An increment is lost: both read the same old value

questions.prompt: All 32 lanes of a warp do atomicAdd on the same shared counter. How many serialised updates does that one instruction cost?
Why does privatising a histogram in shared memory help on uniform data but not on a constant image?
options: Shared memory is slower on constant data
It removes global traffic, but lanes still collide on the same shared counter when values repeat
questions.explanation: Contention moves from L2 to shared memory; it doesn't disappear.

questions.prompt: Which reduce atomic contention on skewed data?
options: Counting runs of equal values in a register before one atomic
Warp aggregation: one lane adds the count of matching lanes
Several copies of hot counters, summed at the end

questions.prompt: const slot = atomicAdd(count, 0, 1); out[slot] = v; builds a compacted list. What's the catch?
options: The output order depends on timing, not on input order
It can't handle more than 32 threads
questions.explanation: Correct and fast, but unordered. A scan gives a stable order (Chapter 3.5).

questions.prompt: How is an operation like float atomicMax built when the hardware lacks it?
options: A compare-and-swap loop: read, compute, CAS, retry if it changed
questions.explanation: atomicCAS is the universal building block.
